name: Food photography
summary: Photographs of dishes made to look edible and honest. A window, a small set and a short lens give shape, steam and texture, and a few props tell where the meal sits.

philosophy.core_thesis: Food is a sensation, so the picture shows texture, steam and light before it shows the plate.
design_principles: Use a 50mm to 105mm macro lens at f/2.8 to f/5.6, with a shallow plane that falls on the front edge of the dish.
Light from the side or behind with one window or a 60cm soft box at 90° to the lens axis; fill with a white card at 1 stop under.
Shoot at 30° to 45° above the plate for a plated dish, or at 90° for a flat lay.
Put 3 to 5 props in the frame, and cut the dish by 10–20% at an edge.
Keep a warm, natural colour at 5000–5600K; protect reds and greens.
Shoot each dish within 5 minutes of plating, and use a stand-in for the first test frames.
anti_patterns: Flash on the front of the dish
Cold blue casts that kill appetite
Too many props that hide the dish
Dry food with no sheen or steam
Plastic or inedible-looking fake food that is claimed as real

composition.framing: Close and tight; the plate is cropped by 10–20% at one edge.
composition.viewpoint: 30° to 45° above the plate; 90° for flat lays; 0° for tall burgers and cakes.
composition.geometry: Triangles of plate, glass and prop; diagonal leaning lines of cutlery or a napkin.
composition.subject_placement: Hero dish on a third, with a lesser prop on the opposite third and a soft background.

principles.rule: Let the hero dish take 40–60% of the frame, with the sharpest plane on its front edge.
Put the hero within 0.05 of 0.33 or 0.67 of the width.
Rank 1 hero, 2 to 3 supporting props and 1 to 2 background items; the hero has the highest contrast and the sharpest plane.
Use 3 planes: a blurred foreground prop at 0.1m, the dish at 0.5m and a soft background at 1.5m.
Set 60% in neutral surface, 30% in the food hue and 10% in a garnish accent.

light.quality: Soft, directional window light, with a small soft box as a stand-in.
light.direction: Side or back-side at 90° to 135° from the lens axis; a white card fills the front.
light.time_of_day: Late morning or early afternoon at a north window

lens_and_camera.format: Digital full frame; macro or short tele
lens_and_camera.aperture: f/2.8 to f/5.6 (f/8 for flat lays)
lens_and_camera.focus: Focus on the nearest edge of the hero; the plane falls off in 2cm.
lens_and_camera.support: Tripod with a side arm for flat lays

colour_and_grade.treatment: Warm, natural colour with a rich red and green and a slight lift in the highlights.
grade_recipe: Set the white balance at 5200K, tint +2.
Set the black point at 3% and the white point at 97%.
Apply +15% midtone contrast and +10% clarity on texture.
Lift red and orange saturation by +10% and keep skin-like tones natural.
Add a soft glow (−10 clarity) to steam and glaze.
Sharpen at radius 0.6px, amount 60%, with a mask on the hero.
colour_and_grade.grain: Low: ISO 100, clean, with a faint 5% grain for a filmic look

subject_and_staging.staging: Full. A food stylist cooks and plates; a prop stylist chooses the board, the cloth and the cutlery.
subject_and_staging.direction: Add motion: pour, tear, dust or drip; shoot 3 to 5 frames at the peak of steam.

workflow: Shoot tethered and check the steam and sheen at 100%.
Stack 2 or 3 focus frames for depth only when needed.
Clean crumbs and spills; keep the real texture.
Export at 4:5 and 16:9, sRGB, 2400px on the long edge.
post_processing.output: A warm, tactile image for a menu, a cookbook or an ad.

emotion.target_response: Appetite and comfort: the viewer wants to eat and to sit at that table.

use_cases: brand campaigns for drinks and snacks
avoid_when: The brief needs a clinical, nutritional catalogue image.
The food cannot be styled within 5 minutes of plating.

modifiers.how: Shoot the cook at work in the kitchen with a 35mm lens at f/4, available light and the real mess; keep the hands.
Use a white backdrop, a diffused window at 2:1 and f/8; reduce saturation by −12% and keep a pale wood board.

sources.title: Francisco de Zurbarán, Still Life with Lemons, Oranges and a Rose (1633), Norton Simon Museum
Helene Dujardin, Plate to Pixel: Digital Food Photography & Styling (Wiley, 2010)
